History of Cellular Jail & Accounts of torture
The Cellular Jail in Andaman, known as 'Kala Pani,' was a brutal British prison for Indian freedom fighters, first used for 1857 revolutionaries like Allama Fazl-e-Haq Khairabadi.
Prisoners endured horrific torture, including forced labor like oil extraction, and severe punishments for defiance, as exemplified by Ullaskar Dutt and Master Chhattar Singh.
